sentence_stem: Had the committee been informed earlier,
correct_completion: the project would have been approved last spring.
full_sentence: Had the committee been informed earlier, the project would have been approved last spring.
acceptable_variants: the project could have been approved last spring.
the project might have been approved last spring.

options.text: the project will be approved next week.
options.why_wrong: The inverted third conditional ('Had + subject + past participle') describes an unreal past situation, so the main clause must use 'would/could/might have + past participle'. 'Will' is a future form and does not match the past condition.

options.text: the project was approved last spring.
options.why_wrong: This is a plain past statement with no conditional meaning. It does not express the hypothetical result of the information that was not given earlier.

options.text: the project would have been approved last spring.
if it were approved last spring.
options.why_wrong: 'If it were' is a second conditional form for unreal present situations. It cannot follow the past condition expressed by 'Had...been informed', and the inversion already carries the 'if' meaning.

grammar_focus: Inverted third conditional (Had + subject + past participle)
explanation: In an inverted conditional, 'Had' replaces 'If' and the subject moves before the past participle. The main clause then needs 'would have' (or could/might have) plus the past participle to describe the unreal past result.
translation: Якби комітет був поінформований раніше, проєкт схвалили б ще минулої весни.
